name: weak-scale-crossing-count-nv
description: Corrects my #6704 claim that the corpus lacks a decay RATE: prop:hadron-half-life states one and its coupling W(q) is derived in closed form (checks 1-3). What is open is the rate's SCALE -- the weak-scale crossing count N_v = 3v/m_e, which is q-independent and, read as a crossing count, must be a positive integer (checks 4-6).
scope: (a) scope-limited. Nothing here derives N_v or refutes any route to it; the integrality check is a necessary condition on the corpus's own crossing-count reading, tested against experiment alone.

checks.name: W_at_one_is_one_quarter
checks.detail: W(1) = 0.25; the classical vanishing of the rate is carried by Q -> 0, NOT by the vertex factor

checks.name: N_v_is_q_independent
checks.detail: mu_0 and E_x cancel between v = N_v E_x mu_0 and m_e = 3 E_x mu_0, so N_v = 3 v/m_e = 1445519.509159468 carries no anchor and no Markov-parameter convention

checks.name: N_v_integrality_measured
checks.detail: N_v = 1445519.509159468 +/- 0.3718; nearest integer 1445520.0, offset 0.490841 = 1.32 sigma. Consistent with integrality -- so the experimental precision does NOT refute the crossing-count reading, and does not confirm it either: the resolution is coarser than the spacing between candidate integers is meaningful.

checks.name: integrality_test_ceiling_is_below_two_sigma
checks.detail: an integrality test is bounded by (1/2)/sigma = 1.34482 sigma here, so NO value of N_v could be declared non-integral at 2 sigma from CODATA 2022. The measured 1.32 sigma is 98.17% of that ceiling -- i.e. N_v sits essentially as far from an integer as it is possible to sit, and the test still says nothing. G_F's 0.5144 ppm is the sole limiting input (m_e contributes 0.31 ppb); a 3-sigma test needs 0.2306 ppm, a 2.2308x tightening.
